# K-210 Plant Air Compressor: Control Narrative
## Section 4: Start, Stop, and Protection

### 4.1 General

K-210 is a three-stage integrally geared centrifugal air compressor driven by a 900 kW, 6.6 kV motor with a soft starter. The operator starts and stops the unit from the DCS. Capacity is controlled by inlet guide vanes (IGV, command ZC-210, position ZT-210) and by the blow-off valve FV-211 to atmosphere. Discharge header pressure is controlled at 7.0 barg.

Lube oil is supplied by a shaft-driven main oil pump and an AC auxiliary oil pump P-212. The vendor control panel supplies the surge line and the surge protection function. Surge protection opens FV-211.

Setpoints in this section are the values given in the design basis. Items marked **[Confirm]** are assumptions to be verified against the vendor documentation or at commissioning.

### 4.2 Operating States

| State | Description |
|---|---|
| Stopped | Motor de-energized, shaft at rest, no start request. |
| Ready | All start permissives satisfied, no trip active. |
| Pre-lube | P-212 running, oil pressure being established. |
| Starting | Soft starter ramping the motor. |
| Loading | Running at speed, IGV and FV-211 under control, taking load. |
| Running | Normal operation, header pressure under control. |
| Unloading | Controlled load reduction before a normal stop. |
| Coastdown | Motor de-energized, P-212 supplying oil until the shaft stops. |
| Tripped | Protective trip latched, reset required. |

### 4.3 Start Permissives

The DCS accepts a start command only when all of the following are true. Each unsatisfied permissive is displayed on the DCS as first-out information.

1. No trip is active, and all trips have been reset.
2. Oil temperature TT-214 is above 25 °C. If it is at or below 25 °C, the tank heater is available to bring the oil up to temperature.
3. Oil header pressure PT-213 has been established by P-212 at or above the normal operating pressure of 2.5 bar **[Confirm: the permissive threshold is not given in the design basis, and the vendor may specify a different value]**.
4. IGV position ZT-210 is at the start position (minimum or closed, per vendor) and FV-211 is fully open.
5. Vibration transmitters VT-215, VT-216 and VT-217 are healthy and below the alarm value.
6. Motor start limits are satisfied (see 4.4).
7. Soft starter reports ready, with no fault. The 6.6 kV breaker or contactor is in service and available.
8. Vendor control panel reports ready, with no active trip.
9. No emergency stop is active.

### 4.4 Motor Start Limits

The motor vendor limits are 3 starts per hour and a minimum of 20 minutes between hot starts. The DCS enforces both as a start permissive.

- The DCS keeps a rolling 60-minute count of starts. A start is counted when the start command is issued. When the count reaches 3, the permissive is withheld until the oldest start is more than 60 minutes old.
- A 20-minute timer starts at each motor stop that follows a run. Until it expires, a hot start is blocked. **[Confirm with the motor vendor the definition of "hot" and whether the 20 minutes is measured from the previous start or from the previous stop. This narrative assumes it is measured from the stop and that any restart after a run is treated as hot.]**
- The DCS displays the time remaining until the next start is allowed and the reason it is blocked.
- The start counters must not be reset by an operator action or by a DCS restart. They are retained in a retentive memory. The ability to override or reset the counters is restricted to a supervisor-level access and is logged.
- A failed start (a start that trips before reaching speed) counts as a start.

### 4.5 Start Sequence

The operator selects Start at the DCS.

1. **Permissive check.** The DCS verifies 4.3. If any permissive is not met, the command is rejected and the reason is displayed.
2. **Pre-lube.** The DCS starts P-212. If PT-213 does not reach 2.5 bar within a time delay of 30 s **[Confirm]**, the sequence aborts, P-212 is left running, and a "Pre-lube failed" alarm is raised.
3. **Pre-lube hold.** After PT-213 reaches 2.5 bar, the DCS holds for a minimum pre-lube time **[Confirm with vendor]** to wet the bearings and gears.
4. **Valve positions.** FV-211 is confirmed fully open and the IGV is confirmed at the start position. The compressor starts unloaded.
5. **Motor start.** The DCS closes the start command to the soft starter. The soft starter ramps the motor to full speed. The DCS monitors the following during the ramp:
   - The motor reaches full speed within the start time limit **[Confirm: soft starter ramp time plus margin]**. If not, a start failure trip occurs.
   - PT-213 stays above the low-low trip value, with the trip logic handled as described in 4.7.
   - Vibration is monitored. Vibration trips remain active, and the alarm is allowed to pass during the acceleration only if the vendor permits a start-up inhibit window **[Confirm]**. No such inhibit is assumed. Trip at 60 µm applies throughout.
6. **Run-up complete.** The soft starter reports end of ramp (bypass closed, if fitted). The DCS moves the sequence to Loading.
7. **Auxiliary oil pump.** The shaft-driven main oil pump now supplies oil. P-212 continues to run until PT-213 is stable at or above 2.5 bar on the main pump, and then stops after a delay of 60 s **[Confirm]**. P-212 is returned to auto-standby (see 4.8) and is not left stopped without auto start armed.
8. **Loading.** The IGV is released to the pressure controller after a warm-up time at no load **[Confirm with vendor]**. FV-211 closes under the control of the anti-surge function. The pressure controller then regulates the discharge header pressure at 7.0 barg using IGV position, with FV-211 trimmed closed.
9. **Running.** When FV-211 is closed and the unit is delivering to the header, the state changes to Running.

The DCS monitors the total start sequence time and raises an alarm if any step exceeds its allowed time.

### 4.6 Normal Stop

The operator selects Stop at the DCS.

1. **Unload.** The pressure controller is taken out of control. The IGV is driven to its minimum position, and FV-211 is opened under the surge and blow-off logic. The unit discharges to atmosphere rather than to the header. The discharge check valve prevents reverse flow from the header.
2. **Unload hold.** The unit runs unloaded for a cooldown time **[Confirm with vendor]**.
3. **Motor stop.** The DCS opens the motor circuit via the soft starter and breaker or contactor.
4. **Coastdown lube.** P-212 starts when the stop command is issued, or at the latest when PT-213 falls below the low alarm value of 1.8 bar. P-212 runs until the shaft has stopped and for a post-lube time **[Confirm with vendor]** afterward. Shaft stop is confirmed by speed or vibration signal or a time delay set from the vendor coastdown time.
5. **Final state.** The IGV is at the start position and FV-211 is fully open. The state changes to Stopped, and the restart timers in 4.4 begin.

The unit must not be restarted while the shaft is still rotating. A restart permissive requires confirmed zero speed **[Confirm: depends on the instrumentation available]**.

### 4.7 Protective Trips

The following conditions trip the unit. A trip is latched. It de-energizes the motor immediately, opens FV-211, drives the IGV to the start position, and starts P-212. The first-out trip is captured and displayed.

| Tag | Condition | Alarm | Trip | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PT-213 | Oil header pressure low | 1.8 bar | 1.3 bar (low-low) | Normal 2.5 bar. Trip uses a short confirmation delay to avoid spurious trips. During start-up the trip is active from the time the motor is started **[Confirm]**. |
| TT-214 | Oil temperature | High alarm **[Confirm]** | High-high **[Confirm]** | Limits taken from vendor data. Low temperature is a start permissive only (above 25 °C). |
| VT-215 | 1st-stage vibration | 40 µm | 60 µm | |
| VT-216 | 2nd-stage vibration | 40 µm | 60 µm | |
| VT-217 | 3rd-stage vibration | 40 µm | 60 µm | |
| – | Emergency stop | – | Immediate | Hardwired. |
| – | Start failure | – | Speed not reached in time | |
| – | Vendor panel trip | – | As received | Includes any vendor-defined motor or machine trips. |
| – | Motor protection | – | As received | Motor relay trips (overcurrent, earth fault, thermal and so on) act directly on the 6.6 kV breaker. |

Notes on the trips:

- **Oil pressure.** On a low-oil-pressure alarm at 1.8 bar, P-212 starts automatically (see 4.8). If pressure continues to fall to 1.3 bar, the unit trips. The auxiliary pump start is intended to recover pressure before the trip is reached.
- **Vibration.** Each stage has its own transmitter, and any one reaching 60 µm trips the unit. A bad-quality or failed transmitter raises a fault alarm. Whether a failed transmitter trips the unit or is bypassed under supervisor authority depends on the project's SIL or voting philosophy **[Confirm]**. The trip signals should be hardwired to the safety or vendor controller as required by the project's safety classification, and not rely on the DCS alone.
- **Trip reset.** A trip is reset only when the initiating condition has cleared, the unit is stopped, and the operator has acknowledged it at the DCS. Resetting a trip does not clear the start counters in 4.4.
- **Trip lube.** After any trip, P-212 is run for the coastdown, as in 4.6 step 4. If the trip was caused by lube oil failure and P-212 cannot restore pressure, the cause must be investigated before restart.

### 4.8 Auxiliary Oil Pump P-212 Logic

- **Manual and Auto modes** are available at the DCS. Auto is the normal mode.
- **Auto start of P-212** occurs on any of the following:
  - Start sequence (pre-lube).
  - PT-213 below 1.8 bar (low alarm).
  - Any trip or stop command, until after shaft stop.
  - Main oil pump failure indication, if available.
- **Auto stop** occurs only when the unit is Running with PT-213 at or above 2.5 bar from the main pump, as in 4.5 step 7, or when the unit is Stopped and the post-lube time has elapsed.
- P-212 fails to start or fails to run: an alarm is raised. If this happens when the unit is stopped, a start is blocked. If it happens while the unit is running, the operator is alerted that backup lube is unavailable. The unit continues to run on the main pump, and a controlled shutdown is recommended **[Confirm per project philosophy]**.
- **Power supply.** P-212 is on an AC supply. The reliability of this supply during a power failure is a consideration. A loss of the AC supply stops the motor as well, and the coastdown then depends on the main pump. If the vendor requires a guaranteed coastdown oil supply, such as an elevated gravity tank or a DC pump, this must be provided. **[Confirm: not in the design basis.]**

### 4.9 Oil Temperature and Heater

- If TT-214 is at or below 25 °C with the unit stopped, the tank heater is enabled, automatically or on operator request, until TT-214 is above 25 °C plus a hysteresis band **[Confirm]**. The heater is then switched off.
- The start permissive for temperature is 25 °C or higher. The heater has its own protection, such as a low oil level interlock, so that it never operates uncovered **[Confirm: oil level instrument not listed]**.
- When the unit is running, the heater is off. High oil temperature is alarmed and tripped as in 4.7.

### 4.10 Surge Protection and Blow-off Valve FV-211

- The vendor controller contains the surge line and the anti-surge function. When the operating point approaches the surge line, it opens FV-211 to atmosphere to move the point away from surge. FV-211 is under the control of the vendor surge function and takes priority over the DCS pressure controller.
- The DCS pressure controller must not command FV-211 closed or the IGV open in a way that conflicts with the surge protection. The vendor logic has priority on FV-211. The DCS receives the surge status and FV-211 position and displays them.
- A surge event is alarmed. Repeated surge events within a set time **[Confirm with vendor]** trip the unit, because repeated surge damages the machine.
- When the header pressure is above setpoint or the demand is low, the surge protection can open FV-211 and vent air. The operator should note that this wastes energy. Where demand is persistently low, the preferred action is to stop the unit, subject to the start limits in 4.4. Frequent stop-start cycling is limited by the motor, which allows 3 starts per hour with at least 20 minutes between hot starts.
- On a trip or stop, FV-211 fails or is driven to the open position. The failure mode of FV-211 on loss of air or signal should be fail-open **[Confirm]**.

### 4.11 Alarms Summary

| Alarm | Setpoint |
|---|---|
| Oil header pressure low (PT-213) | 1.8 bar |
| Oil header pressure low-low, trip (PT-213) | 1.3 bar |
| Vibration high (VT-215/216/217) | 40 µm |
| Vibration high-high, trip (VT-215/216/217) | 60 µm |
| Oil temperature below start permissive (TT-214) | 25 °C |
| Start inhibited, start limit | 3 per hour, or 20 min since the last stop |
| Pre-lube failed | 30 s timeout |
| P-212 failure | On fault or failure to start |
| Surge detected | From the vendor controller |
| Instrument fault | Bad quality on PT-213, TT-214, VT-215/216/217, ZT-210 |

### 4.12 Open Items for Confirmation

1. Definition of a "hot start" and the timing basis for the 20-minute limit, from the motor vendor.
2. Start permissive threshold for PT-213 before start, and the pre-lube time.
3. Oil temperature high and high-high limits, and the oil level instrument.
4. Whether vibration trips are inhibited or delayed during acceleration.
5. Voting and failed-instrument philosophy for PT-213 and VT-215/216/217, and the SIL classification of the trips.
6. Provision for coastdown lube oil on loss of AC power.
7. Zero-speed detection method.
8. Unload and cooldown times, and the warm-up time before loading.
9. Surge repeat trip criteria, and the fail-safe position of FV-211.
10. Vendor panel and DCS interface: which signals are hardwired and which are on the serial link.
